26

30	- the spec under review — `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, its code index in `PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md`
31	- the architecture under review — `ARCHITECTURE.md`

33	- lens histories — `docs/lenses.md`
34	- the queue — `ROADMAP.md`
35

38	`skills/test-author/SKILL.md`.
39

41	
42	A review inside this pack writes its record to `docs/prover/` as `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` and commits
43	it. `guardrails/check-prover-record.sh` is the gate that reads it; `docs/prover/README.md` holds the
44	shape. A record covering a push carries the `PUSH-REVIEW` marker and the fields `Range:`,
45	`Files read:`, `Checks run:`, `Findings:`, and `Blocking:`, each with a value. The record's opening
46	line names the prover version that ran, and the gate's freshness arms hold the record against the
47	last change to each guarded document.
48	
49	A minor (`x.Y.0`) bump of this pack requires a `FULL` pass
50	(`skills/build-pipeline/references/minor-bump-gate.md`).
51	
52	## Pin map
53	
54	Each pack requirement below is carried by the named prover lens. The requirement's text lives in
55	`PRODUCT_SPEC.md`; the lens's mechanics live in the prover. When a lens moves or renames in a prover
56	release, this table is the one place the pack updates.
57	
58	| Requirement | Prover home |
59	| ----------- | ----------- |
60	| INV-114 | How to write findings; Reviewing a rewrite before it merges |
61	| INV-141 | Work that belongs elsewhere; Cross-surface policy uniformity |
62	| INV-30, INV-31, INV-72, INV-138 | Edge-condition completeness |
63	| INV-125 | Cross-surface policy uniformity |
64	| INV-126, INV-127, INV-165, INV-167 | Lifecycle |
65	| INV-72 | Unwritten seams; Interactive overlap across layers; Edge-condition completeness |
66	| INV-136 | Interactive overlap across layers |
67	| INV-128, INV-144 | Three-source disagreement |
68	| INV-49 | False-serialization and over-broad independence edge |
69	| INV-244, INV-248 | Delivery separability along a declared axis |
70	| INV-101 | Declared cross-cutting laws |
71	| INV-169 | The second-sibling question (feature-fit review) |
72	| INV-170 | The quantifier re-verify (new-surface review) |
73	| INV-215 | The cognitive-load lens, its reading-load reading |
74	| INV-233 | The node-growth re-ask (architecture lens) |
75	
76	## Version discipline
77	
78	`scripts/install-external-skills.sh` installs the prover and refuses a version below the minimum in
79	this page's metadata. The installed copy under `skills/product-prover/` is not tracked by this
80	repository; the external repository is its only source of truth. Raising the minimum here is a pack
81	change and lands as one.
82	
83	## The pack's lens bindings
84	
85	This page is written against `live-spec-base` (v5.0.0). The bindings below are the pack-side review
86	duties a live-spec project adds to the external prover's own lenses. The prover's body states the
87	general method; each line here is the pack's concrete pin of one duty, read beside the body on every
88	review run inside a live-spec project.
89	
90	- **Unwritten seams [INV-72].** For every surface the document places before a user, the review walks
91	  every other surface that can be present at the same time and asks what happens at the seam; a
92	  reachable situation with a blank answer is a finding. The reviewer reports the blank and invents no
93	  answer. The headline of this duty is the unwritten seam.
94	- **Entry symmetry (SPEC INV-50).** A conditionally-entered face with no deliberate re-entry path is a
95	  finding, and a written one-way counts as an answer.
96	- **Domain language on every user-facing surface.** The review holds every user-facing string to one
97	  bar: read them as the user would; a leaked internal word is a finding.
98	- **The architecture lens, seven items.** Beside spec-fact ownership and named seams, the review checks
99	  that the quality budgets are stated with their instrumentation homes and watchers — each names its
100	  watcher — that the runtime view walks every promised flow, that the placement view says where
101	  every node runs, and that each grown node re-answers its fitness questions (the node-growth
102	  re-ask).
103	- **Unbacked surfaces and unlabelled sketches.** A surface no requirement backs, or a sketch shown
104	  without its label, is a finding; the stress families of questions in the prover's own reference run
105	  over each.
106	- **Gaps, never taste.** The review's output bar is: Report gaps. Taste is out of scope. What reads
107	  as a preference goes to the design reviewer or the human, never into a finding.
108	- **The norm lens.** An approved prototype cited as `norm: <path>` is the definition the build answers
109	  to; a plan contradicting its own artifact is a finding.
110	- **The record names its reviewer.** Every record closes naming the prover skill version it ran under,
111	  so a spec proven under an old lens set never keeps a silent green.
112	- **The class lens (SPEC INV-124).** The prover's class lens is the document-side face of the
113	  confirmed-bug class hunt: the three questions it asks on a filed defect are how the hunt reaches
114	  the document, and its class line lands in the record beside the other verdicts.
115	- **Member of the review-record class (SPEC INV-156).** The record a review writes under
116	  `docs/prover/` is one member of the review-record class the pack's spec declares once — the shared
117	  dated-file shape every review pass in this pack writes.
118	- **Clean-context release review (SPEC INV-237).** A release of this pack runs its adversarial pass
119	  from a fresh, differently-contexted seat that authored none of the release's changes, and a newly
120	  grown lens or rule is self-applied to its own introducing document before release.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""gen-language-consumers.py — build the language rules' consumers from their one home.

WHAT IT DOES. It reads the language rules and writes the four files that carry them onward — one page
per reader, and the rule text the judging model reads:

  - `docs/language-rules.md` — the WRITER's page. Per rule: the rule sentence, the reader test, the
    surfaces it binds, the examples, the exceptions, the thresholds, and every list the rule names.
    It opens with the six surfaces defined, the block rule, a roster of the rules binding each
    surface, and a legend for the words its companion page uses; it closes with an index that maps a
    writer's question to the rules answering it. Nothing on this page is about machinery.
  - `docs/language-rule-coverage.md` — the MAINTAINER's page. It opens with the status words and the
    arming events defined, the files that carry the rules, and how to run each kind of catcher by
    hand. Then, per rule: its status, what catches a break of it with how far each catcher reaches,
    where each catcher is armed, the rule text the judging model reads, the files that stated the
    rule before the source became its one home, and the notes with their history. A blind reader of
    the single old page skimmed exactly these fields and reported that none of them changes a word a
    writer writes, which is why they live here. The running instructions moved here on 2026-07-28
    from `docs/language-defects.md`, which is the record of where the rules came from and which
    cannot carry a runbook: a reader there met the arming events and the status words with neither
    defined on the page.
  - `hooks/language-laws.json` — the rule text the judging model reads, one body per surface. A rule
    appears in a surface's body when the rule binds that surface and names the model as a catcher.
    Each entry reads `LAW <n> — <the model-facing sentence>`, then the rule's reader test, then its
    exceptions, numbered from 1 inside each surface. `LAW` is the marker the judge's own parser
    matches (`hooks/register_judge_core.py` renumbers on it), so the marker stays as it is while the
    prose around it calls these rules.
  - `skills/text-audit/references/reader-prompt.md` — the COLD READER's page: the prompt a session
    pastes into a fresh reading session. Its hand-written frame stays as written — the title, the
    opening paragraphs, and the closing paragraph. The pasteable block's stop list is generated: one
    bullet per rule whose owner is a skill and which binds the human-prose surface, sorted by rule
    id, each bullet giving the rule's name and its reader test.

It also owns one BLOCK inside each of several hand-written pages:

  - `docs/language-defects.md` — the record of where the rules came from. Its prose is its own; the
    shared words and roles it is written in stand between the `generated:vocabulary` markers and are
    rewritten on every run. A cold reader is handed one page and cannot follow a pointer to another,
    so a word two pages share is defined on both, out of the one home. The same page states how many
    rules the home carries, which identifier is the highest, and how many stand retired; that sentence
    stands between the `generated:rule-home-totals` markers.
  - `skills/text-audit/references/human-prose-rules.md` — the audit skill's rule sheet. Its own prose
    is hand-written; the rules the skill holds a text to stand between the `generated:human-prose-rules`
    markers. The skill ships to a host and the rule home stays behind, so the skill carries the rules
    with it and still has one home for them. Until 2026-07-28 the skill stated seven of these rules
    again in its own words. The block stood inside `skills/text-audit/SKILL.md` until 2026-07-29, when
    the skill body was split to hold the ~500-line ideal.
  - `docs/plans/2026-07-28-top-level-readability.md` — the readability plan. Its opening count of the
    rules and of the ones binding the spec body stands between the `generated:rule-totals` markers.
  - `docs/language-worked-example.md` — the page that walks one text through the human-prose roster.
    The size of that roster stands between the `generated:human-prose-total` markers.

Those last three blocks landed on 2026-08-05. Each held a hand-typed total that drifted every time a
rule was added, folded, or retired: the plan said 54 rules where the home carried 63, and the record
said 53. A number a reader meets in prose is generated here or it goes stale.

WHAT IT READS. `guardrails/language-rules.json`, plus the config files a rule's `lists` field names:
a list entry carrying `source` and `key` is read out of that JSON at build time, so a list a rule
depends on can never drift from the list its checker reads. No rule text, no word list, and no
threshold is held here, so a rule is edited in the source and regenerated.

WHY THIS TEST EXISTS. The prompt handed to a reader who meets a text with no context lives in
`skills/text-audit/references/reader-prompt.md`, where the skill's 2026-07-29 split moved it from the
skill body. Two other places describe that same prompt: the skill's own prose,
which tells a maintainer what the reader does, and `docs/language-defects.md`, which records how a
reading is run. On 2026-07-28 those three drifted: the prompt asked for four parts per stop and said
"Do not guess the missing answer", while the record page said a reading carries the guess the reader
made, and the class-into-rule procedure needed that guess. A blind reader caught the contradiction
after it had stood for two repair rounds. Bringing the prompt into step then left two sentences in
the skill and its README still saying the reader guesses nothing, which the craft review caught.

The settlement on 2026-07-28 was to stop restating the shape in a fourth place. `docs/language-defects.md`
now points at the skill and states no parts of its own, so the shape has one home and cannot drift into
a second reading of itself. That page still relies on the guess, in the step where a stop becomes a
rule, so the test holds the pointer and holds the restatement gone.

WHAT THIS HOLDS. The prompt asks for five parts, the fourth being the reader's guess. The skill's own
prose and its README agree that the reader records that guess. The record page names the skill as the
prompt's home and restates none of the five parts. Any future edit that changes one of these homes
without the others fails here.

Reach: this test opens `skills/text-audit/SKILL.md`, `skills/text-audit/references/reader-prompt.md`,
`skills/text-audit/README.md`, and `docs/language-defects.md`, and reads their prose. It runs no script
and reads no other file.
"""
import os
import re
import unittest

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SKILL = os.path.join(ROOT, "skills", "text-audit", "SKILL.md")
PROMPT = os.path.join(ROOT, "skills", "text-audit", "references", "reader-prompt.md")
README = os.path.join(ROOT, "skills", "text-audit", "README.md")
RECORD = os.path.join(ROOT, "docs", "language-defects.md")


def read(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return fh.read()


class TestReaderPromptShape(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_prompt_asks_for_five_parts(self):
        body = read(PROMPT)
        self.assertIn("write one entry with five parts", body,
                      "the reader-prompt in %s no longer states five parts" % PROMPT)

    def test_the_fourth_part_is_the_reader_s_guess(self):
        body = read(PROMPT)
        self.assertRegex(body, r"4\.\s+the guess you made in place of the missing answer",
                         "the prompt's fourth part no longer asks for the reader's guess")

    def test_the_prompt_asks_for_no_repair(self):
        body = read(PROMPT)
        self.assertIn("Do not fix anything.", body,
                      "the prompt stopped telling the reader to fix nothing")

    def test_the_skill_body_points_at_the_prompt_s_file(self):
        # The split left the body as the reader's way in, so the body names the file the prompt

class TestGeneratedArtifacts(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_scripts_ship(self):
        self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(GEN))
        self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(GATE))

    def test_committed_artifacts_match_a_fresh_generation(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            r = run(GEN, "--out-dir", tmp)
            self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, "the generator refused to build:\n%s" % r.stdout)
            self.assertEqual(read(os.path.join(tmp, "hooks", "language-laws.json")), read(LAWS),
                             "hooks/language-laws.json differs from a fresh build — regenerate it "
                             "with scripts/gen-language-consumers.py")
            self.assertEqual(read(os.path.join(tmp, "docs", "language-rules.md")), read(DOC),
                             "docs/language-rules.md differs from a fresh build — regenerate it "
                             "with scripts/gen-language-consumers.py")

    def test_each_artifact_opens_by_naming_itself_generated(self):
        self.assertIn("GENERATED by scripts/gen-language-consumers.py", read(DOC).splitlines()[0])
        self.assertIn("GENERATED by scripts/gen-language-consumers.py", read(LAWS).splitlines()[1])

    def test_chat_laws_carry_every_rule_the_source_holds_there(self):
        # A body is keyed by the checker that runs the law and the surface it runs on, so every rule
        # the source marks as model-held on chat stands in the chat body of each checker it names.
        held = [r for r in source_data()["rules"]
                if "chat" in r["surfaces"] and r["catchers"]["model"]["status"] != "absent"]
        self.assertTrue(held, "the source marks no chat rule as model-held — the check would be vacuous")
        bodies = json.loads(read(LAWS))["bodies"]
        for rule in held:
            for checker in checkers_of(rule):
                body = bodies[checker]["chat"]
                self.assertIn(rule["catchers"]["model"]["law_text"].rstrip("."), body["text"],
                              "the %s chat body misses %s (%s)" % (checker, rule["id"], rule["name"]))
                self.assertIn(rule["reader_test"], body["text"],
                              "the %s chat body misses %s's reader test" % (checker, rule["id"]))
        for checker, by_surface in bodies.items():
            for surface, body in by_surface.items():
                self.assertEqual([law["number"] for law in body["laws"]],
                                 list(range(1, len(body["laws"]) + 1)),
                                 "the %s body on %s is not numbered from 1" % (checker, surface))

    def test_the_judge_takes_its_two_bodies_from_the_artifact(self):
        # The swap: register_judge_core.py holds the frame and reads its law text from the artifact,
        # filtering out the laws whose home is the reader's own personal layer.
        core = judge_core()
        bodies = json.loads(read(LAWS))["bodies"]
        for constant, checker, surface in (
                (core.UNIVERSAL_CHAT_LAW, "hooks/register-judge.py", "chat"),
                (core.DOCUMENT_REGISTER_LAW, "scripts/preshow-register-lint.py", "human-prose")):
            expected = "\n\n".join(law["text"] for law in bodies[checker][surface]["laws"]
                                   if not law["personal_home"])

## Strongest defect: ownership runs the *other* way — live-spec generates two files that live inside `skills/text-audit/`

The proposal states the dependency contract as "from the host we need exactly three things: (a) path to text, (b) optional lints, (c) a reading-record directory" (`/private/tmp/live-spec-control/skill-classification.md:43-47`). That is not the contract. live-spec's language-rule home *writes into the skill*:

- `/private/tmp/live-spec-integrate-slimdown/wt-base/scripts/gen-language-consumers.py:115` — `READER_PROMPT_REL = "skills/text-audit/references/reader-prompt.md"`, and the comment at `:112-114` says the generator owns **the whole file, frame and all**.
- `scripts/gen-language-consumers.py:111` — `AUDIT_SKILL_REL = "skills/text-audit/references/human-prose-rules.md"`, listed in `SPLICED` at `:124-126`: the generator owns the block between the `generated:human-prose-rules` markers.

And three armed gates hold that ownership:

1. `guardrails/check-language-rules.py:310` defaults `--reader-prompt` to that path; `check_drift` at `:248-257` reds with "*is absent at %s — it is generated output*" and `check_block_drift` at `:279-282` reds with "*is absent … so the block(s) it lends the generator have nowhere to stand*".
2. `tests/test_language_rules.py:161-166` (`test_gate_stays_silent_on_the_real_file`) runs that gate on the real tree with no arguments, inside the CI pytest run (`.github/workflows/gates.yml:38-39`). It is **not** guarded by `external_clone_or_skip` — it goes red, it does not skip.
3. `scripts/check-registry.json:33-38` declares both files as the gate's `reach`; `guardrails/check-named-checks.py:323-327` arm D fails with "*entry %s reaches %s, which the tree does not hold*", and gates.yml:127 runs it.

So the moment `skills/text-audit/` stops being a tracked directory, three gates red — and if the clone *is* installed there, live-spec's generator writes into a gitignored external checkout whose content live-spec pins by commit. Raising one language rule would then require: regenerate in live-spec → commit into the *external* repo → move the pin → re-run. That is a genuine ownership cycle, and the proposal does not mention it anywhere.

## Four more substantive defects

**2. The pin is not resolvable in CI for a local-only repo.** `scripts/install-external-skills.sh` clones `PROVER_URL` over https and the CI step is `gates.yml:33-37`. `~/live-spec-text-audit` does not exist on a GitHub runner. The proposal's own migration step 4 assumes a GitHub repo (`skill-classification.md:40-41, 68-69`), while the night brief explicitly forbids creating one (`/private/tmp/live-spec-control/night-brief-2026-08-17.md:104`). Those two are incompatible: with a local-only home, CI can never install the skill, so the gates in defect 1 red permanently, not transiently. The proposal's own "what breaks between steps" note (`:72-74`) describes only the transient window and misses this.

**3. The tests do not split cleanly.** The proposal sends `tests/test_reader_prompt_shape.py` to the new repo (`skill-classification.md:57-59`) and claims those tests "no longer read anything pack-related except lint paths". False: `tests/test_reader_prompt_shape.py:35` sets `RECORD = docs/language-defects.md` and four assertions at `:80-99` hold that *pack* page — it names the skill as the prompt's one home, restates none of the five parts, and still carries the guess. That test is a cross-repo drift test by construction; it cannot travel whole and nothing in the proposal says what stays behind to prove it.

**4. The slimming cuts text an in-package generator points at.** The plan moves "The cold reader" (~5 150 B) out of the body. But `scripts/gen-language-consumers.py:844` hardcodes into the generated reader-prompt frame: `The body's section "The cold reader" lists the kinds most blocking findings fall into.` The generated file would then point at a section that no longer exists in the body — and fixing it means editing live-spec's generator and round-tripping regenerated output into the external repo. Same cycle as defect 1.

**5. Concurrency hazard with lane A2 (not the sole blocker, but real).** A2's rewrite discipline runs every rewritten sentence through `skills/text-audit/references/rewrite-meaning-check.md` (`night-brief-2026-08-17.md:75, 129`), and A2 merges *after* C in the stated order (`:143`). Extracting the skill tonight removes that file from the tree the A2 workers read.

## What would turn this into ALLOW

Either of these, before any extraction:

- **(a) De-weld first.** Move the two generated pages out of the skill: make `reader-prompt.md` and the human-prose rule sheet pack-owned artifacts (under `docs/`, or under `skills/text-audit-pack/`), with the skill body taking their location as a host input like the lint list. Update `scripts/gen-language-consumers.py:111,115`, `scripts/check-registry.json:33-38`, and re-home `test_reader_prompt_shape.py`'s pack-side assertions into an adapter test that proves the binding without opening the external body. Then the "three things from the host" contract is actually true and the split is clean.
- **(b) Give the pin a CI-resolvable source** — the extraction cannot land with a local-only home unless CI is changed to vendor the skill some other way; a local git repo makes the version floor check work locally but leaves every CI gate above red.

Plus, in either case: land A2 before C, and re-word the migration's "what breaks" note (`skill-classification.md:72-74`), which today understates the breakage by three gates.
